messages.subject: results of fixed effects changing depending on the levels of a factor defining the random effect
parts:
Dear INLA group,

I have hit a strange result, and I suspect I must be missing something fundamental. I have fitted a simple model in INLA, I have a fixed factor "type" and a random effect "pid":

inlamod=inla(formula=dxyz~type+f(pid,model="iid"),data=inladat)

I then actually run the same analysis, using the same values of pid (the random effect), but with reordered levels for pid - note this is exactly the same data, the only consequence should be, say in an analysis where "pid" might have been defining a fixed effect, what would be the corresponding level of "pid" used in the baseline intercept.

#now creating yet another variable in inladat that just has the order of the
#levels reversed - note this is really just the order of the levels, 
#the data itself is exactly the same!!!
inladat$pidX=factor(inladat$pid,levels=levels(inladat$pid)[34:1])
#create yet another pid version, with another re-ordering of the levels of pid
set.seed(123)
sZ=sample(x=1:34,size=34,replace=FALSE)
inladat$pidZ=factor(inladat$pid,levels=levels(inladat$pid)[sZ])
#run models
inlamodX=inla(formula=dxyz~type+f(pidX,model="iid"),data=inladat)
inlamodZ=inla(formula=dxyz~type+f(pidZ,model="iid"),data=inladat)

I actually got different results for the estimated fixed effect of the factor variable "type". 

#check summary of fixed effects - they are different
summary(rwinlamod)$fixed
                mean      sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant     mode kld
(Intercept) 377.7942 46.2734   293.4068 373.9636   476.6643 365.0775   0
typemax      23.7567 33.3646   -41.6344  23.8804    88.3950  24.1098   0
typemed      -0.2188 29.6941   -58.9336  -0.0875    57.7313   0.1933   0
typemin     -25.7760 31.3201   -86.4016 -26.0287    36.1368 -26.6185   0
> summary(rwinlamodX)$fixed
                mean      sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant     mode kld
(Intercept) 363.5188 28.2183   308.0873 363.5062   418.9591 363.4808   0
typemax      41.6673 28.2459   -13.8592  41.6929    97.0034  41.7484   0
typemed       3.4166 28.0261   -51.6364   3.4242    58.3775   3.4425   0
typemin     -37.1459 28.2527   -92.5315 -37.1736    18.3409 -37.2285   0
> summary(rwinlamodZ)$fixed
                mean      sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant     mode kld
(Intercept) 390.6741 33.0750   325.8241 390.6427   455.6467 390.6008   0
typemax      25.3511 28.8421   -31.2830  25.3526    81.9250  25.3577   0
typemed      -3.8388 28.8352   -60.4532  -3.8393    52.7264  -3.8378   0
typemin     -37.5681 28.8401   -94.1871 -37.5703    19.0115 -37.5722   0

This is surprising to me. I redid the same models in lme from package nlme and I get the exact same results irrespective of the order of the levels, as I would have imagined INLA should too? 

#run same models with lme
lme1=lme(dxyz~type,random=~1|pid,data=inladat)
lmeX=lme(dxyz~type,random=~1|pidX,data=inladat)
lmeZ=lme(dxyz~type,random=~1|pidZ,data=inladat)
#check results - the same, as expected 
lme1$coefficients$fixed
(Intercept)     typemax     typemed     typemin 
  357.32870   194.59460    56.48111   -94.30897 
> lmeX$coefficients$fixed
(Intercept)     typemax     typemed     typemin 
  357.32870   194.59460    56.48111   -94.30897 
> lmeZ$coefficients$fixed
(Intercept)     typemax     typemed     typemin 
  357.32870   194.59460    56.48111   -94.30897 

This seems to imply that INLA uses something about the coding of the factor levels in the analysis, which I would have imagined would not be desirable...? What am I missing?

If someone wants to try to replicate, the data (and the models) are here:

https://www.dropbox.com/s/edf5zi8gma9rbii/v4reduxPublicCopy.RData?dl=0

Many thanks for any feedback sent this way.

Tiago

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] results of fixed effects changing depending on the levels of a factor defining the random effect
parts:
Hi Havard,

As per your suggestion, I used a scaled version of dxyz and the results now are consistent across analysis (and in particular say the intercept is consistent with the lme estimate, after getting back to the response scale). I still don't understand why the problem manifests itself as a function of information that the analysis should not use, namely the labels used for a factor defining a random effect. So while I have a solution for the problem at hand, I am missing the overall reason that the problem arose, and hence it's unclear to me what other unforeseen problems might I hit. Are there any situations where the coding of a factor might lead to different results?

This raises additional points potentially relevant for others:

1. Likely my bad, I was unaware of the general requirement that inputs should be scaled. Is that for the response only or also for the independent variables. I can only imagine that many folks do not scale their inputs, in particular the response variable! Does this mean that results from others might have been impacted by this?
2. It would be great if INLA did that scaling internally and then the required back-scaling for reporting results, as the truth is one would like to have all the results on the unscaled scale of the response. Is there a fast way to get results back on the response scale?

Cheers,
Tiago
